name: Cyprus
description: Cyprus offers a compelling relocation destination for expats, characterized by year-round sunshine, a relaxed Mediterranean lifestyle, and a favorable tax regime. Its high safety ratings and welcoming, multicultural society further enhance its appeal for families, retirees, and professionals seeking a high quality of life within the European Union.
longdescription: Living as an expat in Cyprus provides a unique blend of European and Middle Eastern influences, fostering a vibrant multicultural society where English is widely spoken, especially in business and urban areas. The island enjoys a stable economy, primarily driven by the service sector including tourism, financial services, and shipping. Expats can expect a relaxed pace of life, generally lower living costs compared to many Western European countries, and access to a high standard of public and private healthcare and education. While the job market can be limited outside specific sectors, Cyprus attracts entrepreneurs, digital nomads, and investors due to its business-friendly environment and strategic location. The political environment is stable, though historical divisions between the Greek Cypriot south and Turkish Cypriot north persist, with the Republic of Cyprus being internationally recognized.

visas.name: Student Residence Permit
visas.description: The Student Residence Permit in Cyprus is designed for non-EU/EEA citizens accepted into full-time study programs at recognized higher education institutions in Cyprus. It allows international students to legally reside in the country for the duration of their studies and may offer limited work opportunities.
visas.target_applicant: Non-EU/EEA citizens seeking to pursue full-time higher education (diploma, postgraduate, doctorate, or other higher education diplomas) at accredited institutions in Cyprus.
visas.path_to_residency_description: A student residence permit does not directly lead to permanent residency (PR). After completing studies, eligible students can apply for a post-study stay for job-searching or entrepreneurship (up to 12 months in specific cases). The general pathway involves transitioning from a student permit to an employment-based, business, family, or other qualifying legal residence status, and then applying for PR after 5 years of continuous qualifying legal residence. [7, 14]
visas.renewal_conditions: To renew, students must maintain their full-time student status, demonstrate sufficient financial resources, have valid health insurance, and secured accommodation in Cyprus. The renewal application must be submitted one month before the current permit expires. [4]
benefits: Legal residency in Cyprus for the duration of studies.
Opportunity to work part-time under specific conditions.
Potential for family reunification for spouses and minor children.
Pathway to permanent residency after completing studies and meeting further legal residence requirements.
Easier travel within the EU (once residence permit is obtained and subject to Schengen area rules).
required_documents: Duly completed and signed application form (e.g., MEDU2/MEDUM2)
Valid passport (valid for at least 2 years or duration of stay, some sources say 6 months beyond intended stay for visa) [2, 13]
Official Letter of Acceptance from a recognized educational institution in Cyprus, confirming full-time enrollment, program, and duration [4, 9, 13]

Proof of sufficient financial means to cover tuition fees, living expenses, and repatriation for at least one academic year (bank statements/bank letter showing minimum balance of €9,000-€12,000, or €20,000, or €12,000 with full scholarship, often requiring a bank guarantee) [2, 6, 8, 9, 13, 15, 17]
Original medical examinations for Hepatitis B and C, HIV, Syphilis, and Chest X-Ray (Tuberculosis), conducted in the home country (pre-arrival) and in Cyprus (post-arrival) [2, 5, 9, 13, 17]
Certificate of Health Insurance covering inpatient and outpatient care and transportation of corpse, valid for one year [2, 4, 5, 8, 9, 13]
Original clear Criminal Record Certificate from country of origin/residence, issued within the last 3-6 months [4, 5, 9, 12, 13, 17]
Proof of accommodation in Cyprus (e.g., certified rental agreement or title deed, valid for one year) [2, 5, 9, 13]
Four recent passport-sized photographs [5, 12, 13]
Attested copies of academic qualifications and transcripts [5, 12, 13, 19]
Evidence of English language proficiency (if applicable) [5, 12, 13]
Entry Permit (Blue Slip) (after arrival) [2, 9]
Birth certificate (if a sponsor is a legal guardian) [17]
Duly certified parental consent for minors [15, 16]
application_process_steps: Obtain an official Letter of Acceptance from a recognized Cypriot educational institution. [5, 13]

Gather and certify all required documents (passport, academic records, financial proof, medical certificates from home country, police clearance, etc.). Many documents require attestation by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and/or Cyprus Embassy/Consulate in the home country. [9, 13, 15, 19]

The university typically submits the student visa (entry permit) application to the Migration Department on the student's behalf, or students apply at a Cypriot embassy/consulate in their home country. [5, 12, 13, 15]

Attend a visa interview at the Cypriot embassy/consulate if required, and await the entry permit decision (typically 1 month). Students must remain in their home country during entry permit processing. [5, 12, 15]
Upon arrival in Cyprus with the entry permit, register at the District Aliens and Immigration Unit of the Police and undergo medical examinations in Cyprus within 7-10 days. [2, 4, 5]

Submit the 'after arrival' documents (including original entry permit, local medical examination results, Cyprus bank confirmation, rental agreement) and biometrics (photos and fingerprints) to the Civil Registry and Migration Department to apply for the temporary residence permit (Pink Slip). [2, 5, 9]

visas.name: Work Permit for Third-Country Nationals (Standard)
visas.description: The Work Permit for Third-Country Nationals (Standard) in Cyprus allows non-EU/EEA citizens to legally work and reside in Cyprus for a specific employer and job. The process is employer-sponsored and requires a labor market test to ensure no suitable Cypriot or EU candidates are available.
visas.target_applicant: Third-country nationals who have received a job offer from a Cyprus-based employer and meet the required qualifications and income thresholds.
visas.path_to_residency_description: After 7 years of legal residence in Cyprus, individuals may have the opportunity to apply for Cypriot citizenship.
visas.renewal_conditions: The employment relationship must continue, and all compliance requirements must be met. For residence permit renewal, proof of income (e.g., one year of bank statements showing remittances totaling at least €24,000 and a bank balance of at least €6,000) may be required.
benefits: Allows legal employment and residency in the Republic of Cyprus.
Potential path to permanent residency and Cypriot citizenship after 7 years of legal residence.
Spouse and minor children are eligible for family reunification.
required_documents: Application forms (M.58 and M.64 for initial application by employer; M.61 for renewal, after arrival and initial registration)
Valid passport (photocopy, original for verification; valid for at least six months beyond permit duration)
Copy of entry visa to Cyprus and arrival stamp (if applicable)
Employment contract, duly signed and stamped by the Department of Labour of the Ministry of Labour and Social Insurance (minimum two years duration for some categories)
Curriculum Vitae (CV) in English
Copies of official translated academic qualifications or reference letter proving at least two years of relevant professional experience
Employer's declaration covering repatriation costs
Health insurance certificate (covering inpatient, outpatient care, and transportation of corpses)
Original blood analysis results (HIV, syphilis, hepatitis B and C) and chest x-ray for tuberculosis, performed by a specialized doctor
Police clearance certificate / clean criminal record from the country of origin/residence
Proof of accommodation (title deed or rental agreement, duly stamped if valued over €5000)
Proof of sufficient financial means (bank statements, especially for residence permit application after arrival)
Employer's tax clearance certificate
Bank letter of guarantee for repatriation expenses (€350-€850 depending on country of origin)
Biometric data (fingerprints and photo) to be collected upon registration in Cyprus
application_process_steps: The employer applies to the District Labour Offices of the Department of Labour with a job vacancy, initiating a labour market test to confirm no local or EU workers are available.
If the job cannot be filled locally, the employer may submit an application for a non-EU national, and a positive recommendation from the Department of Labour is secured.

The employer submits an application for an entry and temporary residence and employment permit (using forms like M.58 and M.64) to the Civil Registry and Migration Department, through the District Aliens and Immigration Branch of the Police.
Upon approval of the work permit, the employee applies for a Type D entry visa at the Cypriot embassy or consulate in their home country.

After entering Cyprus with the entry visa, the employee must register with the Civil Registry and Migration Department and apply for a Temporary Residence and Work Permit (often called a 'pink slip') within seven days of arrival. Biometric data is collected.
The employee collects their approved residence permit.

visas.name: Work Permit for Companies of Foreign Interests (Business Facilitation Unit / Foreign-Interest Company)
visas.description: This program facilitates the issuance of residence and work permits for highly skilled third-country national employees of eligible 'Companies of Foreign Interests' in Cyprus. It is part of Cyprus' strategy to attract international investment and talent by streamlining immigration procedures and offering various benefits.
visas.target_applicant: Highly skilled third-country nationals (non-EU/EEA) offered employment by a BFU-registered Company of Foreign Interests in Cyprus, who possess a university degree/diploma or at least two years of relevant work experience.
visas.path_to_residency_description: The standard naturalization period for Cypriot citizenship is reduced from eight years to five years for highly skilled professionals employed under the BFU scheme. This period is further reduced to four years if the applicant demonstrates a recognized excellent knowledge of the Greek language.
visas.renewal_conditions: Must maintain minimum gross monthly salary of €2,500. The employer company must maintain its eligibility as a Company of Foreign Interests and work towards a 30% Cypriot/EU workforce ratio over a five-year period. Employees previously on €2,000 gross monthly salary must meet the €2,500 threshold for renewals from January 1, 2027.
visas.tax_implications: Eligible employees may benefit from a 50% income tax exemption on employment remuneration in Cyprus for a period of 17 years, provided their gross annual income exceeds €55,000 and they were not a Cyprus tax resident for at least 15 years prior to commencing employment.
benefits: Fast-track processing for work and residence permits, typically within one month, without a labor market test.
Right to family reunification, with spouses gaining immediate access to the labor market.
Potential 50% income tax exemption for new tax residents earning over €55,000 annually for 17 years.
Accelerated path to Cypriot citizenship (reduced to 5 years, or 4 years with good Greek language knowledge).
Access to the national health system (GeSY).
required_documents: Completed application form (e.g., MBCS4)
Copy of a valid passport (valid for at least 6 months beyond permit, or 12 months in any case)
Copy of the visa used to enter Cyprus and arrival stamp (if applicable)
CV in English
Copies of official translated academic qualifications or reference letter from previous employer proving two years of relevant work experience
Original employment contract of at least two years duration, duly signed and stamped
Official Declaration by the Employer covering repatriation costs
Health insurance covering inpatient and outpatient care, and transportation of corpses

Original medical test results (HIV, Syphilis, Hepatitis B and C, Tuberculosis via chest x-ray) certified by a specialized doctor in Cyprus (some tests may be required from country of origin before arrival)
Original Certificate of Criminal Record from the country of origin/residence (with Apostille or Cyprus Embassy Stamp)
Duly stamped title deed or rental agreement for accommodation in Cyprus
application_process_steps: The company registers as a 'Company of Foreign Interests' with the Business Facilitation Unit (BFU) by submitting required corporate documents, proof of €200,000 investment/foreign participation, and evidence of a physical office in Cyprus.
Once the company is BFU-registered, the employer obtains an entry permit for the employee from the Migration Department or Cyprus embassy (if required).
The employee gathers all necessary personal documents, including passport, academic/experience proof, employment contract, health insurance, and criminal record certificate.
The employer submits the employee's application for a temporary residence and employment permit to the Civil Registry and Migration Department.

Upon arrival in Cyprus (within 7 days if using an entry permit), the employee must visit the Migration Department's central offices in Nicosia to provide biometrics (photo, fingerprints) and signature.
The employee undergoes medical examinations in Cyprus, certified by a specialized doctor, to prove freedom from specific diseases.

visas.name: Digital Nomad Visa
visas.description: The Cyprus Digital Nomad Visa is a residence permit designed for non-EU/EEA nationals who wish to live in Cyprus while working remotely for employers or clients located outside of Cyprus. It enables location-independent professionals to legally reside in Cyprus and contributes to the development of the country's business ecosystem.
visas.target_applicant: Non-EU/EEA nationals who are either employed by a company registered abroad or are self-employed, providing services to clients located outside of Cyprus, and can perform their work remotely using telecommunications technology.
visas.renewal_conditions: Applicants must continue to meet the income, employment, and residency requirements. Renewal applications must be submitted at least one month before the current permit expires.
visas.tax_implications: Digital nomads can become Cyprus tax residents if they reside for more than 183 days in a calendar year (or under the 60-day rule if specific criteria are met and not a tax resident elsewhere). Non-domiciled tax residents may benefit from 0% tax on dividends and interest for up to 17 years. Income up to €22,000 is tax-free, with progressive rates for higher incomes. Digital nomads working for foreign employers are not subject to social security contributions.
benefits: Right of residence in Cyprus for up to 3 years (1 year initial, renewable for 2 more)
Ability for spouse/partner and minor children to reside in Cyprus (without work rights)
Potential for Cyprus tax residency and associated tax advantages (e.g., non-domicile status)
Access to a Mediterranean lifestyle, modern infrastructure, and a safe environment
Travel within the Schengen Area after 90 days of living in Cyprus with the residence permit
required_documents: Completed application form (e.g., Form MIP1/MVIS8)
Valid passport (at least 3 months validity remaining)
Copy of passport page showing last entry into Cyprus
Two recent passport-style photos
Updated CV or résumé
Proof of remote work/employment (e.g., employment contract for employees, business/client contracts for self-employed)
Proof of income (e.g., bank statements, pay-slips, official evidence of salary payment from the last 6 months)
Criminal record certificate/police background check (not older than six months)
Proof of accommodation in Cyprus (e.g., rental contract, title deed)
Private health insurance covering inpatient and outpatient care and transportation of corpses
Medical examination certificate (blood analysis for HIV, Syphilis, Hepatitis B, C) and Chest X-Ray for Tuberculosis (for children under 15, Mantoux Skin Test)
Letter of intent explaining reasons for working and staying in Cyprus
Marriage Certificate and birth certificates for children (if applicable, translated and apostilled/stamped)
application_process_steps: Enter Cyprus with a tourist visa (if applicable)
Gather all required documents
Complete the official application form
Submit the application and documents to the Civil Registry and Migration Department within 3 months of arrival
Provide biometric data (photo and fingerprints)
Pay the applicable government fees
Wait for the application to be processed and approved
Receive the approval and residence permit
Register your local address

visas.name: Permanent Residence Permit under Regulation 6(2) (Fast-Track / Golden Visa Program)
visas.description: The Permanent Residence Permit under Regulation 6(2), often called the 'Fast-Track' or 'Golden Visa' program, allows non-EU/EEA/Swiss nationals to obtain permanent residency in Cyprus through a qualifying investment. It offers an expedited route to long-term residency for investors and their families, with the permit generally issued for life.
visas.target_applicant: Ideal applicants are third-country nationals (non-EU/EEA/Swiss) who are willing to make a significant investment in Cyprus and demonstrate a secure annual income from abroad.
visas.path_to_residency_description: The permit itself grants permanent residency. It provides a pathway to Cypriot citizenship by naturalization after 7 years of legal residence within a 10-year period, with at least 12 months of continuous residence immediately before the citizenship application.
visas.renewal_conditions: Maintain the qualifying investment, continue to receive the minimum applicable annual income, be registered under the national health scheme in Cyprus or covered by private health insurance, and provide annual clean criminal record certificates. The physical permit card is renewed every 10 years, but the status is permanent. Holders must visit Cyprus at least once every two years.
visas.tax_implications: Holders of the permanent residence permit are subject to Cyprus's standard tax regime if they become tax residents. Cyprus offers a favourable tax regime, but the visa itself does not grant special tax exemptions.
benefits: Permanent residency status in Cyprus, exempting holders from immigration entry procedures (e.g., visitor's visa).
Includes spouse and minor children; adult children can also be included under specific conditions.
No requirement for minimum stay in Cyprus, only a visit once every two years to maintain status.
Potential path to Cypriot citizenship after 7 years of legal residence within a 10-year period.
Allows ownership and receipt of dividends from Cyprus companies, and acting as a director.
required_documents: Completed application form (MIP1)
Valid passport copies (applicant, spouse, and children)
Curriculum Vitae for the applicant
Marriage Certificate (if applicable, duly certified and translated)
Children's Birth Certificates (if applicable, duly certified and translated)
Original Criminal Record Certificate (from country of residence and origin, duly certified and translated)
Proof of qualifying investment and payment (e.g., sale agreement, proof of payment transfer from abroad)
Documents to prove annual income from abroad (tax declarations or auditor confirmation)
Health insurance certificate covering inpatient and outpatient care
Non-employment declaration (confirming no intention for salaried employment in Cyprus, with exceptions for company directors/shareholders)
application_process_steps: Make a qualifying investment of at least €300,000 in one of the approved categories.
Gather and legalize all required personal, financial, and investment documents.
Submit the completed application form (MIP1) and supporting documents to the Civil Registry and Migration Department (CRMD) in person or via an authorized representative.
The CRMD examines the application and forwards it to the Minister of Interior for decision.
If approved, the applicant must visit Cyprus within one year to provide biometric data for the residence permit card.
Receive the permanent residence permit card.

visas.name: Permanent Residence Permit (Category F / Passive Income)
visas.description: The Permanent Residence Permit (Category F / Passive Income) in Cyprus is a long-term residence permit designed for non-EU nationals who can financially support themselves and their families through a secure, regular annual income derived from sources outside of Cyprus, without engaging in employment or business within Cyprus. It allows for indefinite stay and serves as a pathway to potential Cypriot citizenship.
visas.target_applicant: Ideal applicants are retirees, individuals with stable passive income (e.g., pensions, dividends, rental income, interest from deposits) from abroad, and financially self-sufficient individuals not intending to work in Cyprus.
visas.path_to_residency_description: Holders of the Category F permit can apply for Cypriot citizenship after legally residing in Cyprus for a total of 7 years within a 10-year period, with continuous residence in the final 12 months before application.
visas.renewal_conditions: The residence permit card must be renewed every 10 years. To maintain the permit, holders must visit Cyprus at least once every two years, continuously meet the minimum secure income requirement, maintain health insurance coverage (if not a GESY beneficiary), and provide a clean criminal record certificate every three years.
visas.tax_implications: Holders have the opportunity to become tax residents of Cyprus, which may grant them various tax incentives, including exemption from worldwide dividend and passive interest income, as well as from profits from the sale of securities.
benefits: Permanent residency in an EU member state.
Indefinite validity of the permit (though the card renews every 10 years).
Inclusion of spouse and minor children in the application.
Access to the General Healthcare System (GESY) in Cyprus.
Opportunity to apply for Cypriot citizenship after a period of legal residence.
Potential tax benefits for tax residents, including exemptions on worldwide dividend and passive interest income, and profits from the sale of securities.
required_documents: Valid passport copy (for applicant, spouse, and children).
Completed application form (e.g., MIP2).
Brief CV for the main applicant.
Original bank account statements from a Republic of Cyprus bank.
Declaration of secured annual income from abroad (original documents and affidavit).
Proof of income documentation (e.g., tax returns, official dividend statements, property rental agreements, pension benefit letters).
Title deed, contract of sale, or rental agreement for accommodation in Cyprus.
Clean criminal record certificate from country of origin/residence (duly certified and officially translated).
Official marriage certificate (with certified English translation, if applicable).
Birth certificates for children (with certified English translation, if applicable).
Proof of health insurance coverage.
Statement confirming no intention to work or engage in business in Cyprus.
application_process_steps: Gather all required documentation, ensuring all foreign documents are translated and certified.
Secure proof of stable and sufficient passive income from abroad.
Complete the official application form (e.g., MIP2).
Submit the application and supporting documents to the Civil Registry and Migration Department in Nicosia, either in person or through an authorized legal representative.
Provide biometric data (photograph and fingerprints) at a migration district unit.
Receive notification of approval and collect the permanent residency card.

visas.name: Family Reunification Residence Permit
visas.description: The Family Reunification Residence Permit in Cyprus allows non-EU citizens who are legally residing in Cyprus (the 'sponsor') to bring their close family members (spouse and minor children) to live with them in the Republic. The program aims to preserve family unity by granting residence permits to eligible family members.
visas.target_applicant: Non-EU citizens who are legally residing in Cyprus for at least two years, hold a residence permit valid for at least one year, and have a reasonable prospect of obtaining permanent residence, wishing to reunite with their spouse and/or minor children.
visas.path_to_residency_description: After five years of legal and continuous stay in Cyprus, family members are entitled to apply for a long-term residence permit, provided they show stable financial means, health insurance, and have not secured residence by fraud.
visas.renewal_conditions: Cannot exceed the sponsor's length of stay or the validity of the sponsor's residence permit. Holders must not remain outside Cyprus for more than 90 consecutive days, as this may result in automatic cancellation of the permit.
benefits: Allows family members to legally reside in Cyprus with the sponsor.
Initial residence permit is valid for one year and is renewable.
After five years of legal and continuous stay, family members may apply for a long-term residence permit.
Spouses may be able to secure employment in Cyprus under the family reunification category.
required_documents: Application Form
Copy of valid Passport/s (with at least 9 months expiration period for family members, and showing a Cyprus entry stamp for applicants already in Cyprus)
Certified copy of Marriage Certificate (marriage must be at least 1 year old and spouse must be over 21)
Certified copy of Birth Certificate for each child under 18 years old (unmarried and dependent)
Original Clear Criminal Record Certificate for family members (over 16 years of age) from country of citizenship and from Cyprus Police

Original medical examination certificates (blood tests for HIV, Hepatitis B and C, Syphilis, and chest X-ray/Mantoux test for children under 6) from a doctor abroad and validated by a specialist doctor in Cyprus after arrival

Valid health insurance policy for the sponsor and each family member (covering inpatient/outpatient care and repatriation of corpse) OR Registration Certificate in the General Healthcare System (GHS – GESY) and private insurance for repatriation of corpse
Title Deed or Rental Agreement and utility bills (to prove suitable accommodation meeting health and safety standards)
Sponsor's employment contract (minimum 18 months duration at time of application)
Sponsor's tax returns (for all years of residence)
Sponsor's certificate of contributions to the Social Insurance Fund (Form YKA B-9)
Sponsor's Income Declaration (for other income sources, if applicable, with affidavit)
Sponsor's bank account statements
Bank guarantee (covering possible repatriation costs, EUR 350-850 per person depending on citizenship)
Certificate of School enrolment/attendance for children (if applicable)
Original entry permit (for procedures after arrival)
application_process_steps: The sponsor, legally residing in Cyprus for at least two years and holding a residence permit valid for at least one year, prepares the necessary documents for an entry permit for family members.
The sponsor submits the application for an entry permit to the Civil Registry and Migration Department in Nicosia.
Upon approval, an entry permit is issued to each family member.
Within 7 days of arrival in Cyprus, family members must contact the Civil Registration and Migration Department to record their registration at the Aliens Register.
Submit the application for the residence permit, including all supporting documents and undergo medical examinations in Cyprus and provide biometrics (photographs and fingerprints).
Pay the relevant application fees and bank guarantee.

visas.name: Temporary Residence Permit (Pink Slip)
visas.description: The 'Temporary Residence Permit (Pink Slip)' in Cyprus is for non-EU/EEA nationals who wish to reside in the Republic of Cyprus for more than 90 days. Officially known as a Temporary Residence Card (TRC) or Temporary Residence Permit for Visitors, it is issued for up to one year and is renewable annually. It allows holders to live in Cyprus as visitors but generally does not grant the right to work in local employment.
visas.target_applicant: Ideal applicants are non-EU citizens with stable, independent income from abroad, such as retirees, individuals with passive income, or families seeking to relocate to Cyprus without engaging in local employment.
visas.path_to_residency_description: Holders of the Pink Slip may be eligible to apply for EU long-term resident status after 5 years of legal residence, subject to absence limits and additional criteria. A path to Cypriot citizenship is available after 8 years of legal residence, subject to physical presence, language, and other eligibility criteria.
visas.renewal_conditions: To renew, applicants must continue to meet the eligibility criteria, provide updated bank statements, a renewed rental agreement, and valid health insurance. No repeat medical or police clearance is typically needed for renewals. Applications must be submitted at least one month before the current permit expires. The permit is automatically cancelled if the holder stays outside Cyprus for more than 90 consecutive days.
visas.tax_implications: If a Pink Slip holder resides in Cyprus for more than 183 days per year, they typically establish Cyprus tax residency. This can open up opportunities for non-domicile status, which offers zero Special Contribution for Defence (SDC) on dividends and interest income for up to 17 years, and no inheritance or wealth tax. Pension income for Cyprus tax residents can also be elected to be taxed at a flat 5% on amounts exceeding €3,420 per year.
benefits: Provides legal temporary residency in Cyprus for more than 90 days.
Renewable annually, allowing for long-term stay.
Allows inclusion of spouse and children under 18 as dependents.
Offers a pathway to long-term resident status after 5 years and Cypriot citizenship after 8 years of residence.
Potential for favorable tax benefits, including non-domicile status for tax residents.
required_documents: Completed application form (e.g., MVIS3, MVIS7, MVIS8 for visitors) for each family member.
Valid passport copy (original + copy), valid for at least 15 months beyond the application date or for the duration of the permit sought.
Proof of accommodation: Rental agreement (minimum one year) or property title deed, certified by a Muhtar or certifying officer and stamped at the tax office.
Bank statements and proof of transfer of sufficient income from abroad to a Cyprus bank account.
Documents proving stable income from abroad (e.g., pension slips, salary slips from foreign employer, rental income, dividends).
Bank guarantee (amount varies by nationality, typically €350-€850 per family member; some nationalities like UK, Switzerland, UAE may be exempt).
Comprehensive health insurance certificate covering hospitalization and outpatient treatment in Cyprus.
Medical examinations (blood tests for HIV, hepatitis B & C, syphilis, and chest X-ray for tuberculosis; required for first-time applicants only).
Clean criminal record certificate from the country of origin or last residence, apostilled/legalized and translated into Greek or English (for first-time applicants).
Marriage Certificate (if applicable, duly certified and translated).
Children's Birth Certificates (if applicable, duly certified and translated).
School enrollment confirmation for children (if applicable).
Passport-size photographs.
Entry visa (if required for nationality) and the most recent Cyprus entry stamp.
application_process_steps: Enter Cyprus on a valid entry visa (if required) or visa-free.
Open a Cyprus bank account and transfer the required initial deposit and stable income from abroad.
Secure long-term accommodation (rental agreement for at least one year or property purchase) and have the agreement certified and stamped.
Gather all necessary supporting documents, ensuring foreign documents are translated and apostilled/legalized.
Book an appointment with the district Immigration Unit of the Aliens and Immigration Service or the Civil Registry and Migration Department.
Attend the appointment in person to submit the application, provide biometric data (fingerprints and photograph), and pay the application fees.
Await approval; applicants are allowed to legally stay in Cyprus while their application is pending.

Citizenship by Descent.desc:
Cypriot citizenship by descent is based on *jus sanguinis* (bloodline). Individuals born to at least one Cypriot citizen parent usually automatically receive citizenship at birth, regardless of birthplace, provided neither parent is an illegal migrant.

**Eligibility for Adults (born after August 16, 1960):**
*   If born after August 16, 1960, and your father was a Cypriot citizen at the time of your birth.
*   If born after June 11, 1999, and at least one parent was a Cypriot citizen at the time of your birth.
*   Proof of direct lineage through birth and marriage certificates is required, and the ancestor must not have voluntarily renounced their Cypriot citizenship.
*   Dual citizenship is permitted.

Naturalization.desc:
Foreign nationals can acquire Cypriot citizenship through naturalization after completing a residence requirement. The standard route typically requires **7 years of legal residence in Cyprus within the last 10 years**, plus a continuous 12-month residency immediately before applying.

**Newer rules (as of March 2026) for highly skilled workers:** Highly skilled workers of foreign companies can apply after **4 or 5 years of residence** if they pass a Greek language test. Level A2 (simple communication skills) grants the right to apply after five years of lawful residence.

General requirements also include proof of good character and proficiency in Greek.

Birthright.desc: Birth in Cyprus alone does not automatically grant citizenship (*jus soli*). Citizenship is generally acquired by birth if at least one parent is a Cypriot citizen at the time of birth, following the principle of *jus sanguinis*. This applies regardless of the child's birthplace.

Spouse and Family.desc:
Foreign spouses or civil union partners of Cypriot citizens are eligible to apply for citizenship.

**Requirements:**
*   Minimum of **3 years of marriage or civil union**.
*   If residing in Cyprus, an additional requirement is **2 years of prior continuous residency** immediately before the application.
*   If residing abroad, the 3-year marriage requirement still applies, but they must demonstrate a genuine and continuing relationship. If married for at least 5 years and have at least one child, a letter explaining the request for citizenship is not necessary.
*   The Cypriot spouse must sign a declaration of harmonious living.
*   Required documents include marriage certificate, applicant's birth certificate, clean criminal record, copies of passports/IDs, and children's birth certificates (if applicable).

tax_advice:
*   **Personal Income Tax:** Taxable income up to €19,500 is exempt from income tax. Progressive rates apply from 20% to 35% for income exceeding €19,500, with the top rate of 35% applying to income above €60,000.
*   **Non-Domicile Status:** Qualifying non-domiciled individuals are exempt from tax on dividends and interest income for 17 years, and there is no inheritance or wealth tax.
*   **Employment Income Exemptions:**
    *   **50% Exemption:** Individuals earning over €55,000 per year who were not Cyprus tax residents for at least 10 consecutive years prior to commencing employment can claim a 50% reduction on their employment income for up to 17 years.
    *   **20% Exemption:** A 20% deduction (limited to the lower of 20% of emoluments or €8,550 per annum) may apply for those earning less than €100,000, provided certain residency conditions are met. This deduction was extended to 2025.
*   **Corporate Tax:** The standard corporate tax rate is 12.5%, one of the lowest in the EU.
*   **VAT (Value Added Tax):** The standard VAT rate is 19%.
*   **Capital Gains Tax:** Generally 20% on the sale of real estate located in Cyprus; gains from the disposal of shares and other financial instruments are typically exempt.
*   **Pension Income:** Foreign pension income can be taxed at a flat rate of 5% on amounts exceeding €3,420 (or €5,000 according to another source) per annum, or at normal income tax rates.
local_tips:
*   **Cost of Living:** Cyprus offers a relatively affordable cost of living compared to many other European countries, though Limassol tends to be more expensive than other cities like Larnaca or Paphos.
*   **Housing:** Renting a one-bedroom apartment in a city center can range from €900–€1,000, while outside city centers it might be €700–€800. For families, three-bedroom apartments can start from €1,700+ in city centers.
*   **Language:** The official languages are Greek and Turkish, but English is very widely spoken, especially in tourist areas, business, and among younger generations, making daily life and business communication easy for expats. Learning some basic Greek phrases is highly recommended for deeper integration.
*   **Safety:** Cyprus is considered one of the safest countries in Europe with low crime rates and rare violent crime. Petty theft can occur in crowded tourist areas, so standard precautions are advised.
*   **Registration:** Expats typically need to apply for a residence permit depending on their purpose (work, education, family reunification, or investment). The process can involve bureaucratic hurdles and considerable paperwork.
*   **Transportation:** Public transportation is limited mainly to buses, and many residents opt for owning a car for greater flexibility. Car insurance and licensing fees apply annually.
*   **Healthcare:** Cyprus offers both public (GESY) and private healthcare options. EU citizens working or living long-term can access GESY after three months, while non-EU citizens may need private insurance initially. Healthcare is of high standard and relatively affordable.
*   **Climate & Lifestyle:** Enjoy over 300 days of sunshine annually and a relaxed Mediterranean lifestyle, ideal for outdoor activities.
*   **Expat Community:** Cyprus has a large and diverse expat community, making up around 20-22% of the total population, facilitating easier social integration.
